newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Banking shares fall on Nigerian bourse.
newsitem.headline: Banking shares fall on Nigerian bourse.

text.p: Shares of some of Nigeria's big banks fell at Wednesday's trading due to huge sell-offs which have continued to depress the market, dealers said.
The all-share index ended at 6892.19, up from 6879.72 on Tuesday.
Dealers said the banks joined some leading manufacturers to end lower as a result of seasonal off-loading by investors, desperate to get cash for year-end expenses.
"Investors usually sell during this period to raise money for the Christmas festivity expenses and children's school fees," one dealer said.
Afribank and Guaranty Trust Bank dropped 20 kobo each to 4.20 naira and 12.30 naira, respectively. Union Bank fell nine kobo to 5.30 naira.
But United Bank for Africa rallied 23 kobo higher at 5.80 naira. NAL Merchant Bank which posted a higher half-year profit on Wednesday ended unchanged at 4.80 naira.
Beverages makers Cadbury slumped by 80 kobo to 23.00 naira in what one dealer described as a "massive off-loading", while conglomerates United African Company closed 7.60 naira, down by 34 kobo down.
Cement shares also ended weaker. Ashaka Cement fell 20 kobo to 17.50 naira while Benue Cement dropped 10 kobo to 7.50 naira.
Oil marketers, however, finished stronger. Mobil was 70 kobo up to 47.70 naira, Unipetrol went 60 kobo up to 54.20 naira while Total ended at 55.80 naira, up by 50 kobo.
Texaco at 32.10 naira, Agip at 21.50 naira and African Petroleum at 42.80 were all up with 49 kobo, 40 kobo and 20 kobo, respectively.
